# ThreadSanitizer suppression list - KEPT NARROW, AND EVERY LINE IS MEASURED.
#
# Run 36063084319 (commit 444f938) was the first time the ThreadSanitizer job
# ran to completion. What it measured:
#
#   test result: ok. 3220 passed; 0 failed   (4270.64 s)
#   WARNING: ThreadSanitizer: data race       x 354
#
# Every one of those 354 reports has `sled 0.34.7` somewhere in its stack;
# not a single report is free of it. The split:
#
#   306  free -> std::sys::alloc::unix::dealloc   (dropping sled objects)
#    48  <sled::pagecache::segment::SegmentAccountant as Drop>::drop
#         (sled-0.34.7/src/pagecache/segment.rs:140)
#
# So the races are not in our concurrency code; they are on the dependency's
# shutdown path: sled leaves its background threads unjoined at close and the
# same memory is touched from both sides while dropping. sled 0.34.7 is the
# last release of that crate and it is unmaintained.
#
# This list silences that known, external noise. What it does NOT silence
# matters more:
#
#   * a race in budlum code is not suppressed: the patterns only match
#     symbols beginning with `sled::`;
#   * the canary runs WITH this list. If ThreadSanitizer stops seeing the
#     deliberately written race, the job fails, so the list cannot hollow
#     out the gate;
#   * `print_suppressions=1` is on, and the job prints how many reports the
#     list swallowed. If that number ever falls to zero the list has become
#     dead weight and is deleted; if it jumps, the cause is read before the
#     number is accepted;
#   * any warning that survives the list is counted, and a non-zero count
#     fails the step.
#
# This file is not the fix. The fix is moving off an unmaintained embedded
# key-value store, which is tracked in issue #80. The list is valid until
# then, and every time it changes the measurement above is taken again.

race:sled::pagecache
race:sled::arc
race:sled::tree
race:sled::context
race:sled::Db
race:sled::ivec
